evaluator: Fictionalized Warren Sack analytical lens; independent holdout analysis only. This evaluator is not Warren Sack, does not speak for him, and provides no endorsement.
evidence: Homepage first viewport (home.png and home.html): the primary navigation exposes About directly, establishing a one-click path from the homepage to the method; the homepage also introduces the operating motif with “Listen. Map. Build. Document. Transfer.”

About page: the method is stated plainly and recursively—“observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue”—and directly links to project evidence.

About page, “Three systems loops”: Harry J. Epstein Company, NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC, and Sunday Dinner/196 are each traced through relationships, system model, interface and social use, and learning or continuity. Additional linked loops cover WOWList and Knowledge Wiki Graphs.

NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC page: lived experience, meetings, sources, questions, and civic actors become a recoverable model; campaign sites, working sessions, town halls, and action pathways become interfaces; running minutes, source maps, question logs, action trackers, and the explicit Align/Translate/Implement/Sustain sequence provide inspectable continuity and handoff evidence.

Sunday Dinner/196 page: two bounded workflow reconstructions show observation and modeling becoming usable participation interfaces—Receive/Orient/Configure/Hand off/Remain available for residencies and Invite/Receive/Host/Document/Continue for gatherings—while public milestones and a credited photograph ground the account.

WOWList page: organizers’ existing language is modeled as followable keyword communities; collaboratively editable natural-language entry becomes the interface; organizer calendars, support materials, an independent tutorial, and a dated 35-city snapshot show social use, adoption learning, documentation, and stewardship.

CallNYC page: constituent-services records are modeled around recognizable issues and district context, implemented as 61 resident-facing pathways, publicly released and iterated, then preserved through a repository, screenshot, reporting, source notes, and an explicit archival handoff.

Knowledge Wiki Graphs page: semantic, evidence, and source-custody responsibilities form a clear information architecture; the proposed pilot moves from knowledge friction and approved sources to a start-here page, decision record, correction path, teammate test, and continue/revise/stop handoff. The CallNYC date correction supplies a concrete recursive learning trace across public surfaces.

Public resume PDF, page 1, distinguishes current and historical web-systems experience and states that historical implementation does not itself establish present proficiency. Page 2 places AI Evals under Education & Professional Development rather than claiming instructor affiliation or certification authority.

The dated Open House material is used as contextual lineage: the About page cites the 2006 public article, preserves collective-participation boundaries, and explicitly rejects structural equivalence, peer-reviewed-research status, completed production deployment, client adoption, and inference of present proficiency.
safety_findings: No material PR-016 public-safety blocker was observed in the reviewed packet.
Collective credit is preserved across Open House, WOWList, FairRentNYC, CallNYC, and Sunday Dinner; the pages avoid sole-authorship, endorsement, mandate, and sole-causation claims.

Historical and emerging systems are status-bounded: CallNYC is archived and unofficial, WOWList’s current surface is a noindex tester threshold rather than a restored calendar, and Knowledge Wiki Graphs is early research rather than production SaaS or a completed client pilot.

Protected participant records, coalition strategy, legal-review material, credentials, private analytics, customer data, and unapproved collaborator material are described as withheld rather than exposed.

No current Max/Jitter proficiency, disciplinary invention, peer-reviewed research, or production-deployment claim appears. The reviewed HTML also contains no phone-number match; the approved number appears only on resume PDF page 1.
recommendation: Pass this PR-016 holdout at 4. The candidate makes the recursive method immediately legible, demonstrates it through more than three bounded and inspectable project loops, and maintains unusually strong distinctions among lineage, present practice, collective work, public proof, protected material, and future proposals. Aggregate this score with the other fresh PR-016 judges before asserting the rubric’s three-judge median or broader launch readiness.
